options.answer: Use plain Promise.all: if any per-item request rejects, the bulk method rejects with that first axios error. On success it resolves `{ data: [...] }` in input order.
options.if_wrong: Items that did succeed are reported as an error. The list is invalidated only in onSuccess (packages/core/src/hooks/data/useCreateMany.ts:203), so it can show stale data until the next refetch, and a user who retries can create duplicates. This is already true today, so it is not a regression.
options.why: This keeps today's behaviour. Without these methods, core falls back to `handleMultiple`, which is a plain `Promise.all` (packages/core/src/definitions/helpers/handleMultiple/index.ts:5). That fallback is called from useCreateMany, useUpdateMany and useDeleteMany. So users already get reject-all today, and the ticket's own Scope line says Promise.all. The response types have only a `data` array and no field for errors (packages/core/src/contexts/data/types.ts:345-371), so a partial result cannot be expressed without changing core types. Every sibling provider that implements these methods uses Promise.all: appwrite, medusa, strapi-v4 and nestjsx-crud. The partial-failure test then asserts that the call rejects with the failing item's error.

options.answer: Use Promise.allSettled and always resolve `{ data: [...fulfilled items] }`, dropping or logging the items that failed. Assert in the test that only the successful items are returned.
options.if_wrong: Real failures are hidden: users see 'Successfully created' while some rows were never written. It also changes behaviour silently compared with the current core fallback.
options.why: This would invalidate the list and show the records that were written. But the return types allow only `data: TData[]` (packages/core/src/contexts/data/types.ts:345-371), so the failures cannot reach the hook. useUpdateMany's error notification (packages/core/src/hooks/data/useUpdateMany.ts:634) would never fire, and the success notification would claim every item worked. Nothing in the ticket asks for partial-success semantics.

options.answer: Use Promise.allSettled, then reject if any item failed, with an error that carries the first failure's `message`/`statusCode` plus the failed ids or indexes, after every request has settled.
options.if_wrong: It adds an error-shape contract that has to be documented and maintained but gives the user nothing in the default UI. If the error is built carelessly it can drop `statusCode`, which would break the existing notification text.
options.why: The call still rejects, as the fallback does today (packages/core/src/definitions/helpers/handleMultiple/index.ts:5), so the hooks' error path is unchanged. It also tells callers which items failed and waits for in-flight requests before reporting. The cost is a custom error shape that no other refine provider uses, and the hooks read only `err.message` and `err.statusCode` (packages/core/src/hooks/data/useCreateMany.ts:262-267), so the extra ids are visible only through custom errorNotification or onError callbacks.

options.answer: Use unbounded Promise.all over every id or variable, as the ticket's Scope line says.
options.if_wrong: Very large selections can hit rate limits or overload the backend, which causes partial failures. The risk exists today and is unchanged.
options.why: This matches the current behaviour: the core fallback already fires every request at once (packages/core/src/definitions/helpers/handleMultiple/index.ts:5). It also matches every sibling provider that implements these methods: appwrite, medusa, strapi-v4 and nestjsx-crud. Users get no more concurrent load than they get today.

options.answer: Cap concurrency at a fixed number, for example 5–10 in flight, using a small in-file worker pool. No new public option.
options.if_wrong: Bulk actions get slower with no request for it, and the code grows beyond what the ticket scoped. Any fixed number chosen is arbitrary.
options.why: This protects backends on large bulk actions. But nothing in the repo asks for it, no sibling provider does it, and it changes timing compared with today's fallback (packages/core/src/definitions/helpers/handleMultiple/index.ts:5). It also needs extra tests, using fake timers per .claude/rules/tests.md.

options.answer: Add an optional `SimpleRestOptions.concurrency` (default unlimited), applied to the three bulk methods.
options.if_wrong: It adds a public option that becomes a compatibility commitment, for a problem nobody has reported.
options.why: The default is unchanged, and the existing `options` parameter (packages/simple-rest/src/provider.ts:54-56, 68) is already a place to put it. But this adds public API surface the ticket did not ask for, which then needs docs, tests and the changeset to cover it.
